svg.title: The identities of a cloud flow
svg.desc: A flow in the centre with five identities around it. Owner: who may edit the flow and receives the platform's notifications; the owner's licence sets the performance profile; a service principal can be the owner. Connection: the identity every action uses; for Dataverse one of three authentication types, OAuth as a signed-in person (not shareable), Service principal with client ID, secret and tenant (shareable), or Client certificate auth with a PFX file and password (shareable); the service principal must exist in the environment as an application user with a security role. Connection reference: the solution component the flow points to; each environment binds it to its own connection. Run as, optional and only on the Dataverse row trigger: Flow owner, Row owner or Modifying user for actions that use the invoker's connection; the flow owner needs the privilege Act on Behalf of Another User. Run-only users: who may start an instant flow, with their own or the embedded connections. Below, the Cedar picture: before, the connection reference cedar_DataverseAutomation pointed to Karim's OAuth connection, so rows were modified by Karim, the role was Karim's and the flows stopped when his access changed; after, it points to a service principal connection of the app registration cedar-automation, application user Cedar Automation with the roles Flow Automation – Cedar and Plug-in Automation – Cedar, rows are modified by Cedar Automation, and the kill switch is to disable the application user.
